findings.highlight: If I start looking for another route now
findings.evidenceJa: 今から乗り継ぎだから
findings.explanation: Setsuna is waiting for the connecting bus and still has a transfer or connection ahead, which may make her later. The translation says she is looking for an alternate route, inventing rerouting rather than an ordinary connection.
findings.japanese:
「そっか…こっちは今、連絡バス待ち。
今から乗り継ぎだから、わたしの方が遅くなるかな…」
findings.todokanai: "Is that so… I'm still waiting for my bus. If I start looking for another route now, I might be late…"

findings.evidenceJa: パリがもう凄い雪でさ
findings.explanation: Haruki has reached the Strasbourg station and says Paris had extremely heavy snow, explaining his delayed arrival. 'Here in Paris' wrongly leaves him in Paris immediately before he takes a taxi to the Strasbourg hotel.
findings.japanese:
「パリがもう凄い雪でさ、
今日中に着かないかと思ったよ」
findings.todokanai: "It's snowing really hard here in Paris. I didn't think I'd make it by today."

findings.highlight: Through my determination… I was able to catch up just in time.
findings.evidenceJa: 俺の決心に、時間がついてきてくれた
findings.explanation: Haruki personifies time as having caught up with or cooperated with his decision, letting the proposal plan come together. The translation says his determination enabled him to catch up to time, reversing the sentence's agent and poetic relation.
findings.japanese: …俺の決心に、時間がついてきてくれた。
findings.todokanai: Through my determination… I was able to catch up just in time.

findings.highlight: I know I've been working hard.
findings.explanation: Haruki silently answers Hamada's formulaic 'thanks for your hard work' with 'Yes… I'm tired,' turning the workplace greeting literal. The translation makes him congratulate himself for working hard and loses the sarcastic call-and-response.
findings.todokanai: Yes… I know I've been working hard.

findings.highlight: will be sent to you in an attached file
findings.evidenceJa: 添付ファイルで送ってあるから
findings.explanation: Hamada says the detailed attachment has already been sent to Haruki's computer email address and orders him to review it. The translation makes the sending future, changing whether the work materials are already available.
findings.japanese:
『詳細はＰＣのメアドに添付ファイルで送ってあるから、
そっちをしっかり見ておくように。
とりあえずこちらは概要だけ』
findings.todokanai: "The detailed information will be sent to you in an attached file via email. I just want to summarize the most important points."

findings.highlight: I just simply don't want to believe it.
findings.explanation: Haruki explains that he merely held the natural assumption that nobody but Setsuna could call his name in this foreign place. The translation replaces that mistaken premise with a conscious refusal to believe what he hears.
findings.japanese: そんな当たり前の思い込みがあっただけで。
findings.todokanai: I just simply don't want to believe it.

findings.explanation: Haruki's stunned geographical calculation gives the Paris-to-Strasbourg express journey as roughly two and a half hours. The translation cuts the stated travel time to roughly two hours.
findings.japanese:
ここはフランス北東部の都市、ストラスブール。
パリから特急で２時間半くらい。
findings.todokanai: This is Strasbourg, a city located in the northeast of France. Taking a trip from Paris to here, even on an express train, would take approximately two hours.

findings.highlight: she went to the same school as you
findings.explanation: Hamada recalls that Kazusa was Haruki's classmate, a same-cohort relationship. The translation only says she attended the same school, weakening the precise past connection at the reveal.
findings.japanese:
『なにしろ取材対象は、
日本人ピアニストの冬馬かずさ。
確か北原の同級生だったよな？』
findings.todokanai: "Because the person you're interviewing is the Japanese pianist, Touma Kazusa. I recall she went to the same school as you, didn't she?"
